stem: An 8-year-old boy was identified during a school-based TB screening program that periodically checks students in the area for symptoms, part of a standing outreach activity; his teacher had noted he seemed unusually tired in recent weeks but hadn't flagged a specific complaint. On questioning, his mother reports about three weeks of intermittent low-grade fever and a mild cough she hadn't thought worth a clinic visit. He has no significant past medical history and his growth has been age-appropriate. No known TB contact in the household. Chest X-ray shows right paratracheal lymphadenopathy without cavitation or miliary pattern. Sputum could not be produced despite coaching, and a gastric aspirate was negative on smear and molecular testing. No HIV risk factors, no suspicion of drug resistance. Exam: well-appearing, no respiratory distress, no palpable lymphadenopathy outside the chest findings on imaging.

patient.social_history: Lives with parents; identified via a school-based screening program rather than by the family seeking care
patient.presenting_complaint: Intermittent low-grade fever and mild cough, noted as unusual tiredness by his teacher
patient.exam_findings: Well-appearing, no respiratory distress, right paratracheal lymphadenopathy on imaging, no palpable lymphadenopathy
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: Generalized tiredness noted only by his teacher, without a specific parental complaint, treated as insufficient grounds for further evaluation
Mild, intermittent low-grade fever attributed to a string of ordinary childhood viral illnesses rather than a persistent process
ntep_correct_actions: Recognize that this child's case was appropriately identified through routine, systematic school-based active case-finding, consistent with standing national program policy rather than a threshold-gated activity.
Start this child, who has non-severe disease without evidence of drug resistance, on the standard 6-month regimen (2HRZE/4HRE); no shorter regimen is offered regardless of severity.

Diagnose this child using clinical judgment: the suggestive imaging pattern together with the negative bacteriological results and supportive clues is sufficient to diagnose clinically-diagnosed TB, without a defined, weighted scoring tool.
who_correct_actions: Treat this kind of school-based screening as conditionally appropriate only where the local TB prevalence has been shown to meet the recommended threshold (approximately 0.5% or higher), rather than as a routine activity applied irrespective of a demonstrated local prevalence.

Start this child on a 4-month regimen (2HRZ(E)/2HR) rather than the standard 6-month regimen, since he is between 3 months and 16 years of age with non-severe TB and no suspicion or evidence of MDR/RR-TB.

Consider using a structured integrated treatment-decision algorithm, which allocates evidence-based scores to microbiological, clinical, and radiological findings, as an option for diagnosing this child's presumptive pulmonary TB rather than relying solely on unstructured clinical judgment.
us_correct_actions: Attribute this child's case identification to contact investigation following a known TB contact rather than population-level active case-finding; a routine school-based screening program of this kind is not the primary case-finding model in this framework.
critical_error_conditions: Withholding any TB treatment from this child on the grounds that bacteriological confirmation was not obtained, despite suggestive imaging and an appropriate clinical diagnostic pathway.
expected_divergence_points: Whether this child's school-based case-finding pathway reflects standard, unconditional national program policy or is only appropriate where a threshold local prevalence is demonstrated
Whether a 4-month or 6-month regimen is used for non-severe paediatric TB
Whether an unstructured clinical-judgment approach or a structured, scored treatment-decision algorithm is used to diagnose bacteriologically-unconfirmed paediatric TB
